extracted.intended_audience: general readers and mathematicians seeking an overview of the Clay Mathematics Institute (CMI)
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive Wikipedia article summarizing the Clay Mathematics Institute's mission, governance, major programs (Millennium Prize Problems, fellowships, awards), activities, and publication/access policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Millennium Prize award condition
rubrics_metrics.description: For each problem, the first person to solve it will be awarded US$1,000,000 by the CMI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes CMI established the Millennium Prize Problems on May 24, 2000; the seven problems are regarded as 'important classic questions that have resisted solution over the years.' The list of the seven problems (P vs NP; Hodge conjecture; Poincaré conjecture — solved; Riemann hypothesis; Yang–Mills existence and mass gap; Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness; Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture) defines the scope of awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official problem statements as evaluation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For each problem, the Institute had a professional mathematician write up an official statement of the problem, which will be the main standard against which a given solution will be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solutions are to be judged against the Institute's official statement; adherence to that statement is the benchmark for evaluating whether a claimed solution resolves the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criterion for Millennium Problems
rubrics_metrics.description: The seven problems are considered by CMI to be 'important classic questions that have resisted solution over the years.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMI drew a parallel to Hilbert's problems when selecting these; the implication is that problems chosen are historically significant and long-standing unsolved questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clay Research Fellowships: duration and target
rubrics_metrics.description: Research fellowships range from two to five years and are aimed at younger mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 2024 Clay Research Fellows Ishan Levy and Mehtaab Sawhney were completing their PhDs and started five-year fellowships on July 1, 2024. The fellowships are a postdoctoral program supporting Clay Research Fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clay Research Award: recognition standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual prize recognizing major breakthroughs in mathematical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is given 'in recognition of major breakthroughs in mathematical research.' The article lists many past recipients, illustrating the award is targeted at significant research contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMI activities target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The institute organizes summer schools, conferences, workshops, public lectures, and outreach activities aimed primarily at junior mathematicians (from the high school to the postdoctoral level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This communicates an evaluative/operational focus: programs and outreach are principally designed for junior-level participants rather than established senior researchers or non-mathematical audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMI publications availability policy
rubrics_metrics.description: CMI publications are available in PDF form at most six months after they appear in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a policy limiting immediate open access to publications for a period (up to six months), relevant to those seeking to access CMI-published materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance and grant decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: The institute is run according to a standard structure comprising a scientific advisory committee that decides on grant-awarding and research proposals, and a board of directors that oversees and approves the committee's decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the institutional decision-making standard: the scientific advisory committee makes recommendations/decisions on grants and proposals while the board provides oversight and final approval.
